learningObjectives: Select and justify application settings feature in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

elements.description: Application Settings externalize environment-dependent values such as endpoint addresses and resource settings. Configure typed settings and useful categories, reference them from integrations, and resolve the appropriate environment values at runtime. Avoid hard-coded QA URLs in migrated rules; settings are configuration, not permission to expose secrets.

elements.text: Worked example: A shipping connector uses an endpoint setting with separate Development, Staging and Production values. After migration, verify both the selected environment and the resolved address using a synthetic test request.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Migration equals configuration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Exporting a connector changes its hard-coded URL automatically.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Reference environment-aware settings and validate them on the target.

examPitfalls.title: Settings versus credentials
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Put every credential in a public setting label.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An integration has different URLs in QA and Production. Which design avoids changing its rule for every deployment?

options.text: Reference an Application Setting with environment-specific values
Hard-code the QA URL permanently
Change the case urgency on release
Copy a new connector for every operator

practiceQuiz.rationale: Application Settings centralize values that vary by environment rather than requiring rule edits for each promotion.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After promotion, calls still go to QA. Which check is most direct?

options.text: Check only the portal icon
Increase the SLA goal
Reset every user's worklist
Inspect the resolved environment setting and connector reference

practiceQuiz.rationale: The reference and selected environment determine the endpoint. Visual or routing changes do not correct it.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are useful properties of Application Settings design?

options.text: Unrestricted publication of secrets
A new case type for every address
A value type appropriate to the resource
Categories that group related settings

practiceQuiz.rationale: Types help represent values correctly; categories help find and maintain related settings.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Several integrations share an external host. What is an advantage of referencing configuration rather than literals?

options.text: The setting creates all SOAP mappings automatically
The relevant environment value can be maintained centrally
Calls no longer need authentication
External systems cannot fail

practiceQuiz.rationale: Configuration reduces scattered edits. It does not remove authentication, failure handling or data mapping.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which task validates an added integration resource setting?

options.text: Resolve it in the target environment and test a safe request
Look only at its category name
Assume export changes every URL
Hide all error logs

practiceQuiz.rationale: A setting's presence does not prove correct resolution or connectivity in the target environment.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A resource setting contains a port number. Which design principle applies?

options.text: Always use a case's status as the port
Derive the port from urgency
Create a ruleset for each digit
Use the supported value type matching the resource rather than an unrelated value

practiceQuiz.rationale: Typed settings express the resource configuration clearly and avoid unrelated business fields.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why should a setting reference be used instead of a hard-coded server name in a migrated rule?

options.text: Work queues are always environment-independent
Settings automatically grant admin access
The server name can differ between environments
Rules cannot contain strings

practiceQuiz.rationale: Environment-dependent resource addresses are the core motivation. Settings do not grant administrative rights.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An endpoint is configured correctly. What requirement still needs separate configuration?

options.text: A new operator for each response field
Authentication to the external service
A new browser theme for every call
A ruleset skim after each request

practiceQuiz.rationale: An address establishes where to call; authentication establishes the permitted caller. They are separate integration concerns.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
